walk.title: Solve it: rebuild Harvest Lane's order sheet
walk.sample: Tolu's Orders_final_2 tab · order HL-0043 for Mrs Adebayo · two Mrs Ades

steps.say: This is Tolu's real order tab. It was built for Tolu's eyes, so it breaks every automation. We'll rebuild it so machines, and Tolu, can trust it.
show: Two customers both called Mrs Ade

steps.say: Go rule by rule. There's a title above the headers, several products crammed into one cell, and an amount column mixing text and numbers.
show: Rule 2: "2 tomato, 1 tatashe" in one cell

steps.say: There's a total row and a blank row inside the data, VIP shown only by colour, and no IDs, so the two Mrs Ades are the same person to a machine.
steps.data: phones lost zeros · 4 spellings of paid

steps.say: Everything with its own identity gets its own tab: customers, products, orders, and the items inside each order.
Each tab has an ID in column A, and the many side stores the ID of the one side. Orders point to a customer; items point to an order and a product.
Now formulas, in row two, filled down. The customer's name is looked up by ID, with a clear message if it's not found.
The order total is calculated, never typed: add up the line totals that belong to this order, then the delivery fee.
Notice the unit price is stored on each item, not looked up. Prices change, and last month's orders must still show what the customer actually paid.
Load order HL-0043: one Orders row and two item rows. The total should match our hand calculation from Module 0.3.
Now the Mrs Ade test. Look up order HL-0045 by name and you might get the wrong lady. Look it up by customer ID and it's always the one in Mokola.
steps.data: by ID: right address every time

steps.say: Finally, lock the inputs. Status becomes a dropdown that rejects anything else, because a machine sees Paid and paid as different words.
Phones become plain text so the zero survives, yes or no fields become checkboxes, and the formula columns are protected so nobody types over them.

walk.end: One table per job, IDs for every link, totals that calculate themselves: that's a sheet every automation in this course can read and write.
